title: Vernon Home Energy Rebates 2026: BC Hydro Electricity, FortisBC Gas
desc: Vernon rebates for 2026 from BC Hydro, FortisBC and CleanBC, with Census housing numbers for a city of 19,795 households.
badge: Heat pumps up to $4,000 for electric homes
lead: Vernon runs on BC Hydro electricity and FortisBC gas. Which of the two heats your house decides which rebates you can claim.
cards_heading: What you can claim in Vernon in 2026
cards_intro: Amounts come from the program pages we re-read on October 2, 2026. Each card is a maximum, and most depend on how your home is heated.

cards.title: Whole-home heat pump
cards.note: Must replace electric heat such as baseboards or an electric furnace, meet 100% of the heating load at -5C and be installed by a Home Performance Contractor Network member.

cards.title: Partial heat pump
cards.note: For a heat pump that covers at least half of the heating load while replacing electric heat.

cards.title: Limited-time bonus
cards.note: Extra money on heat pump installs completed between August 1 and October 31, 2026.

cards.title: Income-qualified switch from gas, oil or propane
cards.note: CleanBC pays by income level (Level 3 / Level 2 / Level 1) for a central or three-head heat pump, for invoices from July 6, 2026.

cards.title: Insulation
cards.note: Attic, wall and basement or crawlspace work, paid per R-value added per square foot. Homes heated mainly by electricity only.

cards.title: Windows and doors
cards.note: $100 per opening, with a U-factor of 1.22 or lower.

cards.title: Heat pump water heater
cards.note: Only when it replaces an electric water heater.

cards.title: Solar panels
cards.note: $1,000 per kW, capped at half the cost, from an HPCN member installer.

cards.title: Battery storage
cards.note: Up to $1,500 on its own with solar, or up to $5,000 with Peak Saver enrolment.

cards.title: EV charger
cards.note: 50% of a new wall-mounted Level 2 charger, plus $200 for a power-management device.

sections: A Vernon house heated mainly by electricity can claim up to $4,000 for a whole-home heat pump, up to $5,500 for insulation, up to $2,000 for windows and up to $1,000 for a heat pump water heater from BC Hydro.

FortisBC supplies gas. BC Hydro will not rebate a heat pump that replaces gas. Income-qualified households can use CleanBC at $3,500, $7,000 or $13,000. FortisBC also lists insulation, window and thermostat rebates for gas customers.

The 2021 Census counted 19,795 households. 43% live in homes built before 1981, 48% in detached houses and 66% own. 3,835 are owner-occupied detached houses built before 1981, and 5.8% reported needing major repairs.
Which first: insulation, windows or heat pump

For a pre-1981 Vernon house on baseboards, the heat pump saves the most heating energy, but insulation is cheaper and makes the heat pump smaller. A practical order is attic first (up to $900 from BC Hydro at $0.02 per R-value added per square foot, minimum R12 added), then walls or basement if accessible, then the heat pump. Windows come last because the $100 per opening rebate is the smallest return.

For a gas house, the same order applies, but the heat pump step is available only through CleanBC income help.

BC Hydro gives six months from the invoice date to apply. The installer must be a member of the Home Performance Contractor Network for insulation, heat pumps and solar. If you rent the house out, the BC Hydro account holder applies or signs a consent form. Keep dated photos before and after the work in case you are asked for them.
The January average low is -4.8°C and the record in 2015 to 2024 was -27.2°C. Solar gets about 3.57 peak sun hours a day.

claim_steps: Check whether your heat is electric or gas.
Take insulation and heat pump quotes from HPCN installers.
Check CleanBC if income is lower.
faq: What if I heat with gas?
CleanBC may help by income. BC Hydro will not pay the heat pump rebate.
The record low in 2015 to 2024 was -27.2 degrees Celsius.
